data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism contradicts the very defense it is supposed to support. The claim defends Popper by reinterpreting the preference as selecting 'the most informative surviving conjecture'—a criterion based on logical content (what the theory excludes), requiring no induction. But the mechanism states the preference is instead 'based on... the severity of tests passed, which indicates high informational content.' This substitutes an empirical track-record criterion for a logical-content criterion. Using past test performance to rank or select theories is precisely the reliance on past success that the claim's own first countercondition admits would 'smuggle in induction.' The mechanism never establishes why severity of tests passed 'indicates' informational content—it simply asserts the connection, and that connection is itself an inductive inference (from testing history to a property of the theory). Furthermore, the mechanism's final sentence is circular: 'The reason this holds is that [restatement of the claim], which is what the mechanism above establishes.' No independent reason is provided; the defense is question-begging.
